hint: The famous fact is $\lim_{u \to 0} \frac{\sin u}{u} = 1$. Make the bottom match the inside of the sine.

hints.text: The famous fact is $\lim_{u \to 0} \frac{\sin u}{u} = 1$. Make the bottom match the inside of the sine.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up with $\frac{\sin(2x)}{x}$: write it as $2 \cdot \frac{\sin(2x)}{2x}$. The fraction heads to $1$, so the limit is $2$. Same move with $3$.
Multiply top and bottom by $3$: $\frac{\sin(3x)}{x} = 3 \cdot \frac{\sin(3x)}{3x}$. Let $u = 3x$.
As $x \to 0$, $u \to 0$, so $\frac{\sin u}{u} \to 1$ and the limit is $3 \cdot 1 = 3$.

explanation: With $u = 3x$, the fraction is $\frac{\sin u}{u}$, which heads to $1$ as $u \to 0$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Calculator check (radians!)
steps: The values climb toward $3$. In degree mode you would get nonsense — this limit only works in radians.
